ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A large triangle is divided into four smaller triangles and three quadrilaterals by three straight line segments. The sum of the perimeters of the three quadrilaterals is $25 \mathrm{~cm}$. The sum of the perimeters of the four triangles is $20 \mathrm{~cm}$. The perimeter of the original triangle is $19 \mathrm{~cm}$. What is the sum of the lengths of the three straight line segments?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The outer outline in the figure is a large triangle; inside are drawn three straight line segments, whose endpoints are on the boundary of the large triangle, and which divide the large triangle into several small regions. The problem states that these small regions include 4 triangles and 3 quadrilaterals. Then reason: Let the sum of the lengths of the three internal straight line segments be S. Adding the perimeters of all 7 small regions gives 25+20=45 centimeters. In this total, each segment of the outer boundary of the large triangle is counted only once in total, so it contributes the original triangle perimeter of 19 centimeters; while each internal dividing segment lies on the boundary of two adjacent small regions, so each internal segment is counted twice, contributing a total of 2S. Therefore 45=19+2S, solving gives 2S=26, S=13 centimeters.

method.method_draft: Use global perimeter double-counting. Let S be the sum of the lengths of the three drawn interior segments. From the text, the total of all small-region perimeters is 25 + 20 = 45 cm, and the original outer triangle perimeter is 19 cm. When summing all small-region perimeters, each outer boundary piece is counted once in total, while every interior dividing segment is counted twice, once for each adjacent region. Therefore 45 = 19 + 2S, so S = 13 cm.

method.method_draft: Use a cutting-and-separating interpretation. From the image, view the three straight segments as cut lines inside the large triangle: one from the top vertex to the base, one from the left side to the right bottom vertex, and one from the left bottom vertex to the right side. If the triangle is cut apart along these three segments, the resulting separate pieces are the four small triangles and three quadrilaterals. From the text, the total perimeter of these separated pieces is 20 + 25 = 45 cm. Before cutting, the outside boundary contributes 19 cm. The extra perimeter created by cutting is exactly two copies of each of the three cut segments, because each cut produces two new exposed edges. Thus the added perimeter is 45 - 19 = 26 cm, which equals twice the desired sum, so the sum is 26/2 = 13 cm.
